slot.brief: Ask which of given substances acts as a protective colloid (lyophilic protecting lyophobic) — e.g. gelatin.

stem: Lyophobic sols are easily coagulated by electrolytes. Which of the following substances acts as a protective colloid to prevent their coagulation?

verdicts.working: Protective colloids are lyophilic (solvent-loving) colloids that coat lyophobic sol particles and stabilize them against electrolytes. Gelatin is lyophilic and is the classic protective colloid (cf. gold number). As2S3 and Fe(OH)3 are themselves lyophobic sols; AlCl3 is an electrolyte that causes coagulation.

working:
Lyophobic sols (such as metal sulfides and hydroxides) are inherently unstable and readily coagulate upon the addition of electrolytes. 

When a lyophilic sol is added to a lyophobic sol, the lyophilic particles form a protective sheath around the lyophobic particles, shielding them from coagulating ions. The lyophilic colloid used for this purpose is called a protective colloid.

Among the given choices:
- Gelatin is a lyophilic colloid with high protective power (very low gold number, $\approx 0.005\text{--}0.01\ \text{mg}$).
- Arsenic sulfide and ferric hydroxide are lyophobic sols that require protection and cannot act as protective colloids.
- Aluminium chloride is an electrolyte that induces coagulation (acting as a flocculating agent via $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions by the Hardy–Schulze rule).

Hence, gelatin acts as a protective colloid.
